briefing:
The Fernhollow CRM migration is moving toward a planned go-live of the new CRM on Friday 19 November 2027. The approved project budget is $333,000, and the vendor implementation contract is worth $60,500. Working days are Monday to Friday, and there are no public holidays in this period.

On the technical side, the data migration is scheduled to end on Wednesday 3 March 2027. Joaquin Novak owns the data cleansing workstream, and a data-quality checkpoint is set for Monday 9 August 2027. Svetlana Delacroix owns the integration testing workstream, which sits alongside the cleansing effort and depends on the quality of the migrated records.

User acceptance testing can begin 5 working days after the data migration ends. That rule comes straight from the plan, and the sources do not add anything further on the point, so the briefing leaves it as stated.

Several other workstreams have named owners. Freya Takahashi owns the user training workstream, and the trainer briefing is on Tuesday 6 April 2027. Kwame Iyer owns the reporting dashboards workstream, while Marisol Raman owns vendor management and therefore holds the relationship behind the implementation contract.

Two changes were made in March. The steering group approved a reduction of $46,000 to the project budget, and an additional 33 user licences were approved. The plan itself provides for 360 user licences. The status updates and emails do not reconcile these items beyond what is recorded here, so they are reported as they were received.

Four risks are being tracked. Late fixes from the vendor could delay the go-live of the new CRM, and incomplete customer data mappings could also delay the go-live of the new CRM. Low dashboard adoption could affect the budget. Licence price increases could affect the number of user licences, which links that risk to the licence position described above.

The steering committee meeting is on Tuesday 23 November 2027. That is the formal forum where the outcome of the go-live and the status of these risks and workstreams will be discussed, and the owners named above are the people to whom each area is attributed in the current records.
